purpose: Lets a user enter multiple lines of free-form text, such as a message, description, or comment. Use when the expected content may exceed a single line. For short, single-line values like names or email addresses, use an Input instead.

props.name: label
props.description: The visible label for the field. Always required — a field without a label is inaccessible.

props.name: rows
props.description: Initial visible row count. Sets the starting height without constraining the user from resizing.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Hint text shown when the field is empty. Must not replace the label.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: When set, puts the field into an error state and displays this message below the textarea. Must explain what went wrong and how to fix it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field. Prefer hiding it or explaining why it is unavailable.

variants.name: default
variants.whenToUse: Any time the user needs to enter text that may span more than one line, such as a message body, bio, or description.

variants.name: error
variants.whenToUse: After the user has submitted or left the field and the value fails validation. Always pair with an errorMessage that explains what went wrong.

states.name: default
states.description: Resting state. Neutral border, white background, resize handle visible.

states.name: focus
states.description: Keyboard or pointer focus. Border and outline shift to the focus-ring token.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Non-interactive. Uses disabled surface and text tokens, not-allowed cursor, resize removed.

states.name: error
states.description: Validation has failed. Border and message use the error token. aria-invalid is set.

antiPatterns.never: Omit the label prop or replace it with only a placeholder.
antiPatterns.because: A placeholder disappears on input, leaving the user unable to recall what the field asked for. Screen readers announce the label, not the placeholder. A field without a label is inaccessible.

antiPatterns.never: Set resize: none on the textarea.
antiPatterns.because: Users resize textareas to fit their content. Removing that control is an imposition that serves the layout, not the person typing. Vertical resize is permitted by default; only remove it on disabled state where interaction is already blocked.

antiPatterns.never: Use a Textarea for a single line of text such as a name, email, or search term.
antiPatterns.because: A tall, resizable field sets the wrong expectation about how much text belongs there. Use an Input for short, single-line values.

antiPatterns.never: Show an error state before the user has had a chance to interact with the field.
antiPatterns.because: Pre-emptive errors feel punishing and create anxiety. Validation should fire on blur or submit, not on mount.

antiPatterns.never: Set raw colour or spacing values on the textarea.
antiPatterns.because: Unbound values are invisible to the design system and to an agent reading it. Always bind to a token.

keyboard: Tab moves focus into the field
Enter inserts a newline — it does not submit the form
accessibility.focus: Native focus order. Visible 2px focus ring on :focus-visible using the focus-ring token, offset by 2px. Focus ring colour shifts to error token when in error state.
aria: aria-describedby points to the error message element when errorMessage is set
label is always associated via htmlFor/id — never use aria-label as a substitute for a visible label
accessibility.contrast: Error red on white meets WCAG AA 4.5:1. Disabled text on disabled surface meets WCAG AA 4.5:1 for the default token set.

agentNotes: Default rows to 4 unless the surrounding context suggests a specific amount of content — a comment box warrants more rows than a bio field on a compact form. Enter inserts a newline in a textarea; it does not submit the enclosing form. If the form needs a submit on Enter, that belongs on the Button, not here.
